notes:
Summary: CartSpring is an e-commerce platform for niche D2C brands. Primary pain: search relevance falling during seasonal spikes (4x traffic), current stack = Elastic + heuristic rerank. Wants embeddings + learned reranker with tight cost SLA. Key metrics: target throughput 3k qps peak (spike), steady-state 500 qps; index size ~10M SKUs, avg SKU text ~600-1,000 tokens after product copy + attributes. Latency targets: p50 < 35ms for retrieval, p99 < 120ms end-to-end for rerank path. Cost sensitivity: internal goal <$0.002 per query (including retrieval + rerank).

POC notes (shorthand):
- Using small sample (100k) for initial eval; need realistic token distribution to validate KV cache and batching.
- Rerank approach: dense embeddings for recall -> lightweight learned reranker for ordering; fallback to BM25 on failure.
- Concern from infra: embedding index size & memory footprint during rebuilds (holiday reindexing). Want auto-sharded routing and warm caches.
- CISO: require audit logs + KMS integration; asked for retention controls and residency guarantees for EU customers.
- Product team: wants A/B canary for holiday rollout + automated fallback to cheaper model when cost threshold breached.
- Quote from head of search: "Quality is great but cost during spikes is our blocker — need a predictable unit cost model."

Artifacts: pricing deck + security FAQ shared (drive links), Fireflies transcripts noted. SE recommended Redwood Optimize for batching suggestions, quantization for dedicated pools, and routing policies to spill to cheaper variants under load. Next: run dedicated POC with reserved capacity simulating 4x spike, produce perf + cost per query report. Blockers: legal wants an on-prem appendix (may be satisfied with private deployment addendum) and finance wants committed ARR number before Oct procurement vote.
